column3: Outdoor cushions⏎The outdoor fabric resists water and sun, but cushions last longest when they are kept dry. Water can work in through the seams, so cover the cushions or bring them in when the piece is not in use. After rain, stand cushions on edge so the water drains, and let them dry fully before sitting on them. Blot spills straight away and wash gently with a mild soap solution, and keep harsh chemicals away. The covers are machine washable; follow the care label. In the off season, bring cushions in or store them somewhere dry.⏎⏎Teak frame⏎Left untreated, teak weathers naturally to a soft silver-grey. To clean, wash with mild soapy water and a soft brush, rinse and let it dry. Do not use a pressure washer, which raises the grain. If you prefer to keep the honey colour, a teak protector or sealer can be applied; this is optional, never required.⏎⏎Seasonal storage⏎Cover the piece or store it in a sheltered, dry place through harsh winter weather.⏎⏎A Note on Natural Variation⏎Teak is a natural material, and every piece varies in grain, tone and small markings. Its colour shifts outdoors over time, from honey toward silver, which is part of its character.

column3: Outdoor cushions⏎The outdoor fabric resists water and sun, but cushions last longest when they are kept dry. Water can work in through the seams, so cover the cushions or bring them in when the piece is not in use. After rain, stand cushions on edge so the water drains, and let them dry fully before sitting on them. Blot spills straight away and wash gently with a mild soap solution, and keep harsh chemicals away. The covers are machine washable; follow the care label. In the off season, bring cushions in or store them somewhere dry.⏎⏎Teak frame⏎Left untreated, teak weathers naturally to a soft silver-grey. To clean, wash with mild soapy water and a soft brush, rinse and let it dry. Do not use a pressure washer, which raises the grain. If you prefer to keep the honey colour, a teak protector or sealer can be applied; this is optional, never required.⏎⏎Seasonal storage⏎Cover the piece or store it in a sheltered, dry place through harsh winter weather.⏎⏎A Note on Natural Variation⏎Teak is a natural material, and every piece varies in grain, tone and small markings. Its colour shifts outdoors over time, from honey toward silver, which is part of its character.
